title: Stephan's Quintet - A mammoth cosmic collision (Hubble view)
caption: Stephan's Quintet, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Stephan's Quintet · constellation Pegasus · about 300 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble close-up shows the central part of Stephan's Quintet, a group of galaxies caught up in a gigantic collision. Strangely distorted shapes, lanes of dust crossing from one galaxy to another, and long streams of stars and gas stretching far from the center all point to violent encounters.

The quintet is the prototype of a class called compact groups of galaxies, and astronomers have studied it intensively for decades. The pull of gravity between the galaxies, known as tidal interaction, has bent them out of shape and drawn them together. ESA describes the area as one of the most exciting star-forming regions in the local Universe.
Stephan's Quintet is also popular with amateur astronomers, who know it as a tough target even for good hobby telescopes. Hubble's view reveals the tangled detail that small telescopes cannot show.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.61 x 2.50 arcminutes) and distance (300 million light years), the frame spans roughly 315,000 × 218,000 light-years. Its light set out about 300 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a natural-color composite from Hubble's WFPC2 camera. Red shows light through a filter at 814 nm, green through a filter at 569 nm, and blue through a filter at 450 nm.
understand.eye: Because it uses red, green and blue filters, this image approximates natural color, but the galaxies are far too faint to see in such detail by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image was built from archival Hubble observations, a mosaic of two WFPC2 pointings made in December 1998 and again in the middle of the following year. The group lies about 300 million light-years away in the constellation Pegasus.
alt: Several distorted galaxies close together, linked by dust lanes and long streams of stars and gas.
